question_text:
80% of residents in a particular suburb oppose the construction of traffic lights at a particular intersection. A survey of 20 randomly selected residents is conducted.

Find the probability that:

subparts.solution:
Let $X$ be the number of residents who oppose the construction.
$n = 20$, so $X = 0, 1, 2, 3, \dots, 20$, and $p = 80\% = 0.8$
$\therefore X \sim \text{B}(20, 0.8)$

$\begin{aligned} P(X = 16) &= \binom{20}{16} (0.8)^{16}(0.2)^4 \\ &\approx 0.218 \end{aligned}$

subparts.stem: 16 or more residents oppose the construction

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up binomial cumulative probability $P(X \ge 16)$ with $n = 20$ and $p = 0.8$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The binomial cumulative distribution function computes the probability of obtaining a range of successes in $n$ independent Bernoulli trials.
step_by_step: Set up the lower bound as $16$ and upper bound as $20$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing lower bounds, such as using $X > 16$ ($X \ge 17$) instead of $X \ge 16$.

subparts.stem: between 10 and 15 residents oppose the construction

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up binomial cumulative distribution $P(10 \le X \le 15)$ with $n = 20$ and $p = 0.8$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The probability that a binomial random variable falls in an interval $[a, b]$ is $P(a \le X \le b) = \sum_{k=a}^b \binom{n}{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}$.
step_by_step: Input lower bound $10$ and upper bound $15$ into technology.
Round the calculated result to three significant figures: $0.370$.

subparts.stem: more than 8 residents support the construction.

mark_breakdown.desc: Interpreting the condition that more than 8 support means 8 or fewer oppose, setting up $P(X \le 8)$ with $n = 20, p = 0.8$

subparts.solution:
If more than 8 residents support the construction, then 8 or fewer residents oppose the construction.
Using technology:
$$\text{BinomialCD}(0, 8, 20, 0.8) \approx 1.017288 \times 10^{-4}$$
$$P(X \le 8) \approx 0.000102$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Complementary events or perspective shifts in binomial distributions require adjusting either $p$ or the inequality condition.
step_by_step: Recognize that the condition corresponds to $P(X \le 8)$.
Use a GDC to calculate the cumulative probability with lower bound $0$ and upper bound $8$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting the scientific notation power ($10^{-4}$) displayed on the calculator.
